title: Capstone: Image Editor
description:
An image is a grid of pixels in one heap buffer. This one is shown in the terminal as ASCII art, darkest to brightest: ` .:-=+*#%@`.

```
Circle on a gradient, 40 x 20:
  ..::--==++**##%%@@@@%%##**++==--::..
  ..::--==++**##@@@@@@@@##**++==--::..
```
hints: Pixel (x, y) lives at index `y * width + x` in the buffer.
Brightness is `(r + g + b) / 3` (0–255). The character is `ramp[brightness * 9 / 255]` with `const char* ramp{ " .:-=+*#%@" };`.

A filter makes a copy, changes the copy and returns it. Because `Image` holds a `unique_ptr`, returning it moves the buffer instead of copying it (lesson 7.05). Give `Image` a copy constructor that copies the pixels so the copy at the start of a filter works.
requirements: `struct Pixel { std::uint8_t r, g, b; };` and `class Image` that owns a `std::unique_ptr<Pixel[]>` of width × height pixels
`Pixel& at(int x, int y)` and a `const` version
Drawing: fill, a rectangle, a horizontal gradient, a filled circle
Filters that return a **new** image: grayscale, invert, flip horizontally
`printAscii(const Image&)` that turns each pixel's brightness into one of the ten characters
stretch: Save the image as a PPM file (`P3`, plain text) that image viewers open, and draw a Mandelbrot set.
